subject: Request: availability carve-out & order-form language for on-prem connector
messages:
From: Mike Olson <mike.olson@vitalcore.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@vitalcore.io
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Availability carve-out for on-prem connector and order form language

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A quick follow-up from procurement: VitalCore will be moving a portion of our inference load to an on-prem connector that sits behind our firewall. Our security team requires us to limit any SLA obligations that depend on Redwood-hosted routing for that workload. In practice that means we need an \"availability carve-out\" for the on-prem connector in the order form / exhibit, and a short definition of operational handoffs for escalation (who owns on-call, what telemetry we must provide).

Can you share proposed language we can redline? We also need the MSA/SOW attachments that reference the carve-out so our legal team can run it alongside the rest of the contract. Ideal timeline: internal review by Friday, 9 Apr.

Thanks,
Mike Olson
VP Ops, VitalCore Health
attachments referenced: internal network diagram (we'll share after NDA)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Olson <mike.olson@vitalcore.io>
Cc: contracts@vitalcore.io, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability carve-out for on-prem connector and order form language

Mike —

Appreciate the clear ask. Yes, we can provide an order-form exhibit that defines an \"On‑Prem Connector Carve‑Out\" and a short SOW appendix that documents operational handoffs. Attached are three files: a short SLA addendum draft, an exhibit you can paste into the order form, and an SOW appendix with telemetry/diagnostic expectations.

A few clarifying points so we get language right:
- The carve-out as drafted limits Redwood's availability commitments for requests that enter the system via customer-managed on‑prem connectors where Redwood has no ingress control. In other words the carve-out only applies when the connector endpoint is customer‑hosted and the root cause is inside the customer's network.
- We propose a joint-run escalation matrix (Level 1/2 vendor contacts + customer on‑call) and a minimum set of telemetry (error rates, ingestion timestamps, request ids) to be emitted to a secure S3 share or support portal for troubleshooting.
- If VitalCore wants Redwood to operate the connector on your behalf (managed on‑prem service), we can discuss a separate managed-run SLA instead of a carve‑out.

If that looks aligned I'll loop in Kimberly on the procurement/order form wording and Ben for the tech ops bits.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.pdf; OrderForm_OnPrem_Exhibit.docx; SOW_Appendix_OnPrem.pdf

Kimberly / Ben —

Fwd'ing VitalCore's request and the draft attachments I sent. Could you please:
- Kimberly: review the attached order-form exhibit and SLA addendum for procurement/legal; propose any alternate phrasing if the carve-out is too permissive. VitalCore expects to return redlines by Fri 9 Apr.
- Ben: confirm the telemetry list in the SOW appendix is realistic (low-overhead, PCI/PHI-safe), and add any ops SLAs we should keep (e.g., triage window for Redwood-hosted routing issues).

I'd like to keep the language tight: short definitional carve-out + an operational handoff table. VitalCore is regionally sensitive (EU), so call out data flow and telemetry storage in the exhibit.

Thanks —
Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Mike Olson <mike.olson@vitalcore.io>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability carve-out for on-prem connector and order form language

Hi all —

Thanks Jordan. Quick legal/procurement note and an initial proposed clause below. Ben, I flagged two telemetry items for PHI review (we'll need to ensure the S3 share is scoped correctly).

Proposed order-form exhibit summary (draft):
1) Title: On‑Prem Connector Availability Carve‑Out (Exhibit X)
2) Scope: Applies only to requests for which Customer's on‑prem connector is the ingress point and where the root cause of unavailability is within Customer‑managed infrastructure or network.
3) Effect on SLA: For affected requests, Redwood's availability and latency SLOs set forth in the MSA are excluded; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to assist with diagnosis but will not owe service credits for disruptions attributable to Customer on‑prem infrastructure.
4) Operational Handoff: Joint escalation matrix with named contact roles (Customer on‑call, Redwood Level 1 support, Redwood Platform Ops), expected response/triage windows (e.g., 2 hours triage for P0s during business hours), and required telemetry (request id, timestamp, error code, sample platform traces).
5) Data Handling: Telemetry shared for troubleshooting must be limited to non‑PHI fields unless explicitly permitted in a separate Data Processing Addendum. Telemetry retention for troubleshooting purposes is 30 days unless otherwise agreed.

Ben — can you confirm the sample SOW appendix wording is implementable (low overhead) and propose any concrete triage timing?

Mike — we attached the three files to this message (Redwood_SLA_Addendum_Draft_v1.pdf; OrderForm_OnPrem_Exhibit.docx; SOW_Appendix_OnPrem.pdf). If that aligns, please send any redlines back by end of day Fri 15 Apr (I can compress timeline but wanted to give your legal review some breathing room).

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Procurement, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | kimberly.park@redwood.ai
